- EPS exceeded expectations, reaching $1.39 against a forecast of $1.23.
- Revenue fell short of projections, coming in at $20.15 billion.
- Stock price dropped by 4.18% in pre-market trading.
- Net income stood at $4.9 billion.

- Revenue: $20.15 billion, a decline from forecasted $20.75 billion.
- Earnings per share: $1.39, up 16% year-over-year.
- Net income: $4.9 billion.
- Shareholder returns: $4.8 billion through dividends and buybacks.
## Outlook & Guidance
Looking forward, Wells Fargo anticipates net interest income to rise by 1-3% in 2025 compared to 2024, with expectations currently at the lower end of this range. The bank also projects modest loan growth in the latter half of 2025, while maintaining a focus on efficiency and strategic investments.

ceramic.snippet: Q&A Summary Adrienne Yih (Barclays) asked how Nike can get performance success to halo over Sportswear while pulling back inventory and struggling with full-price sell-through there. Bob Drbul (BTIG) asked about scaling the Nike Mind shoe and where Hill is most excited in the innovation pipeline over the next 6-18 months. ceramic.snippet: Q&A Summary Peter Grom (UBS) asked what category growth and market share are embedded in the flat-to-slightly-up organic sales outlook and whether the slower start improves. Linda Rendle said the outlook assumes muted category growth similar to fiscal 2026 (continued value-seeking) plus continued market-share progress from turnaround businesses, and characterized fiscal Q1 as a timing blip (largely Kingsford), with back-half trends resembling fiscal 2026s sequential improvement. 2025 Annual Report CEO Letter 

Dear Shareholders, 

As I reflect on 2025, I am pleased to review a year of important achievement, strategic advancement, and renewed momentum at Wells Fargo. Since 2019, the management team has led a transformation of our company. This year we achieved a critical milestone: the Federal Reserve’s lifting of the asset cap in June 2025, a restriction that had constrained our growth since 2018.
